findings.title: LFI Vulnerability with Bypassable Directory Traversal Protection
findings.description: The post.php endpoint is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion (LFI) via the 'id' parameter. The application implements directory traversal protection that can be bypassed using double URL encoding (%252e%252e%252f). Additionally, null byte injection (%00) causes file_exists() to fail with a PHP warning, revealing the internal file path structure. A base64-encoded string 'e0knbV9hX1NjcmlwdF9LaWRkaWV9' was found in the page header, decoding to '{I'm_a_Script_Kiddie}'. File upload functionality at /posts/upload-article.php accepts PHP files which are stored but not executed.
findings.evidence: Base64 header: e0knbV9hX1NjcmlwdF9LaWRkaWV9 decodes to {I'm_a_Script_Kiddie}. LFI bypass: post.php?id=%252e%252e%252f%252e%252e%252f%252e%252e%252fetc%252fpasswd bypasses traversal detection. Null byte injection triggers: 'Warning: file_exists() expects parameter 1 to be a valid path, string given in /var/www/html/post.php on line 13'

reproduction.expected: File contents should be included/read, but null byte causes file_exists() warning
